Commentary.Commentary: That's it then from the second Test match between Pakistan and Australia. The three-match series remains deadlocked at 0-0 and the focus now turns to Lahore for the final Test match of the series. That match starts on Monday the 21st of March and the first ball will be bowled at 10.30 am IST (5 am GMT). The build up though will begin much sooner as usual. Do join us then. Till then take care and goodbye!

Babar Azam, captain of Pakistan is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH for his sensational knock of 196 runs in the second innings. He says that the plan was simple, that they had to bat throughout, session by session. Tells that they wanted to build partnerships and continue it. Says that the team showed effort and it was great. Mentions that they had the belief and they stuck to that. Informs that they had a complete focus that they will each session no matter what. States that the way Mohammad Rizwan played, in the end, was outstanding as well to save the game. On being asked where he would rate this knock, he says that he just looked to play till the end as his team needed this knock.

Australia skipper, Pat Cummins says that the wicket was pretty good on Days 4 and 5 and they just couldn't convert those half-chances in the field and it was a good game of cricket overall. Mentions that Mitchell Swepson was fantastic on debut and his figures don't do him justice and applauds Nathan Lyon for his effort as well and mentions that he is proud of the boys. Adds that the way they batted and the way they hunted those wickets in the first innings is a big positive for them going into the final Test match at Lahore.
Presentation ceremony...

Earlier in the match, Australia scored a mammoth 556/9 on the back of a superb 160 from Usman Khawaja in the first innings. In reply, Pakistan were bundled out for just 148 runs with the Aussie players spitting fire. The Aussies then declared on 97/2 in the second innings with a lead of 505 runs. Chasing 506 to win, the hosts went on to show grit and held on to their nerves to finish on 443/7. The match ended in a DRAW! Stay tuned for the presentation.

Mohammad Rizwan is up for a quick chat. He says that obviously batting five sessions against a top team is a big thing. Tells that the way Australia put up an effort was outstanding as well. Mentions that they kept playing with confidence. Informs that Babar and he planned to go for the chase but it was an old ball and they had to play through. States that the plan was simple and that they had to play five sessions. Credits Abdullah Shafique and Babar Azam for playing brilliantly. Says that there was pressure but they had to work hard and they did that. Adds that everyone knows Babar is a top-class player and he does not need to say a lot about him. Ends by saying that it was not easy to bat for two days as Australia always play to win. Says that they will try to play their best in the next game as well.

The pitch in Karachi was a flat one too but the Aussie bowlers showed their class as they got the ball to reverse in the first innings and were halfway home with that bowling performance. They didn't enforce the follow on and batted for a bit but once again started brilliantly with the ball. The pitch though showed its true colours and late on Day 4, Aussie pacers just couldn't get the ball to reverse enough to trouble the opposition batters. Day 5 was a whole match in itself. The visitors couldn't pick up wickets and kept on losing their advantage. Just when it looked the captains were about to shake hands, Babar Azam in search of a double-ton fell victim to Nathan Lyon who never gave up. Once Babar got out, Faheem Ashraf followed suit and Lyon was spinning a web all over the opponents. He then got his fourth wicket as Sajid Khan was dismissed while trying to have a bit of fun. At that point, Australia almost pulled it back but some sensible batting from Nauman Ali and counterattacking play from Rizwan meant that the visitors had to settle for a draw.

After getting bundled out for just 148 runs in the first innings and chasing 506 runs to win the Test match, the hosts were staring down the barrel of defeat. They were not helped by the fact that the in-form batters, Imam-ul-Haq and Azhar Ali departed early in the second innings. Then came the saving grace on Day 4 as skipper Babar Azam put on a 150-plus run stand with Abdullah Shafique to get his side into a much more comfortable position at the end of Day 4. The pair went on to add a total stand of 228 runs before Shafique got out. They were still hanging by a thread at the point and Fawad Alam fell too. Then came in their most prolific player in the last year or so, Mohammad Rizwan. Slowly but surely the hosts began to take the sting out of the chase and frustrated the Aussie bowlers. Babar went on to surpass Michael Atherton's score of 185 to set the highest individual score by a skipper in the fourth innings of a Test match but fell 4 short of a double ton and the hosts lost a couple more wickets in the blink of an eye. Rizwan kept his cool, scored a century and made sure his team didn't lose the match.

What a riveting final hour of sumptuous cricketing action! After all the drama and the action over the course of 5 hard-fought days, neither team has been able to force a result and the second Test match of the series also ends in a DRAW. Unlike the first Test, there was a chance of either side actually getting a win until late on the final day. Overall, Australia will be disappointed to have let the match slip and on the other hand Pakistan will be very pleased as they managed to turn adversity into strength and saw the match through.

FOUR! THAT'S IT! Players shake hands and walk off. Pakistan cling on to a draw. Credit to Australia for toiling so hard and not giving up. Kept everyone on toes till the very end. What a riveting last hour we had, it had everything but then no body deserved to lose and both the teams settle for a draw in the end. Flatter and on off, Mohammad Rizwan stays back and blocks it out.

CENTURY! Mohammad Rizwan scores his second Test ton and becomes only the second Pakistan wicket-keeper to score a ton in the fourth innings! Take a bow! Steps out to this loopy ball and gets a leading edge towards covers but he scampers through to bring up his ton. He has played a match-saving innings here! Raises his hands, takes his helmet and acknowledges the applause from the crowd as well as his teammates,
Is that a Run-Out? Mohammad Rizwan scampers back and puts in the desperate dive to get back to his crease. The third umpire checks the replay and Rizwan is safe. He lives on at 99.

Is Mohammad Rizwan safe? Yes, he is shows the replay. Mohammad Rizwan steps out and gets to the pitch of the ball. He pushes it back to Nathan Lyon who has a shy at the striker's end. However, Mohammad Rizwan makes it back with a desperate dive.

FOUR! Short and turning into Rizwan on the off stump, he goes on the backfoot and whips it with power, gets it past the silly mid on and short mid-wicket, runs all the way down to long-on for another boundary. Rizwan on 99 now!
Short and on off, Mohammad Rizwan goes back and defends.
FOUR! Mohammad Rizwan moves to 95! Lyon overcooks this one, on off. Mohammad Rizwan sees an opportunity and does not back away. He creams his drive through covers for a boundary.
Flatter ball, on off. Mohammad Rizwan defends.
That's a brave leave! Into the rough, outside off. Nauman Ali shoulders arms.
A low full toss, outside off. Ali pushes it to mid off.
Flighted delivery, outside off. Nauman Ali puts a big stride forward and blocks.

FOUR BYES! That took off from outside off, turning into Nauman who was getting behind to defend but misses, Alex Carey has no chance of stopping that and the ball runs all the way down to fine leg for a boundary.
Floats it up, outside off. Ali keeps it out.

Well, apart from Steven Smith and the bowler no one else seemed interested but at this stage Pat Cummins might as well go for it. The third umpire checks the replay and there doesn't seem to be any bat involved. The same is confirmed by UltraEdge as there is a flat line when the ball passes the bat.

Marnus Labuschagne bowls it full and into the rough, outside off. Nauman Ali presses forward and look sto defend with an angled bat but misses. Appeal for caught behind but the umpire says no. Steven Smith at first sli[ is very excited as he thinks he heard something. UltraEdge shows there is no bat involved. Australia burn their review.
With just 3 overs left in the Test match, Pat Cummins has thrown the ball to Marnus Labuschagne.

DROPPED! Usman Khawaja what have you done? Loopy ball outside off, Rizwan reaches out for it and looks to drive but he chips it in the air to mid off and Khawaja doesn't get his hand underneath it but he spills that one in the end. Straight in and straight out but Usman Khawaja makes a meal out of it. What a twist that would have been had he grabbed it!
A full toss again, on the pads. Mohammad Rizwan kneels and sweeps it to deep square leg. It squirts past Lyon as the bal spins away and they scamper through for a brace.
Full and on leg, Mohammad Rizwan gets forward and clips it but the silly mid on fielder does well to stop it.
A low full toss, on the pads. Mohammad Rizwan gets that away as he works it to deep mid-wicket for a brace.
Full and spraying down leg, Mohammad Rizwan goes for the hard sweep this time but misses.
Short and sliding down leg, Mohammad Rizwan kicks it away with his pads.
Quicker delivery, on middle. Nauman Ali gets right behind the ball and defends it from the crease.
Full and on off, defended out again.
Tossed up, on off. Ali presses forward and blocks it out. Nauman Ali is doing very well here.
Short and on off, Ali goes back and blocks.
Outside off, turning away. Ali lunges forward and keeps it out.
Drops it short, on off. Nauman Ali defends it off the back foot.
Loopy ball, outside off. Mohammad Rizwan chips it uppishly to mid off. Nauman Ali back on strike. 5 overs left and 3 wickets to win for Australia!
Shortish, on middle and leg, keeps low as well. Mohammad Rizwan goes deep and whips it to mid-wicket.
Full and outside off, pushed to silly point.
Sliding in on leg, Mohammad Rizwan tries to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads.

SIX! That's a freebie! A full toss down leg, Mohammad Rizwan gets low and picks it up. He hammers it to deep square leg. Goes off the top edge but still goes the distance. He moves to 87!

Quicker delivery at 94.5 kph. Nauman Ali blocks it out.
Tossed up, on off. Ali keeps it out to the off side.
Flatter and quicker, outside off. Nauman Ali presses forward and blocks it out.
Full and on off, driven straight towards short cover and Rizwan cannot take the single to retain the strike.
Ooh, a bit of turn and that could have been it! Around off, the ball just stops in the pitch a bit and Mohammad Rizwan ends up getting a leading edge which falls safe around the cover region.
Swepson goes quicker and fuller. Rizwan manages to keep it out.
Slower through the air, drifted onto the pads. Rizwan defends it out.
The call is for two and they get it with ease. On off and skidding through. Rizwan rocks back and works it through extra cover, into the deep for a brace.
Tossed up, full and on middle. Rizwan jams it back towards the bowler.
Nauman Ali walks out to bat. Mitchell Swepson comes back into the attack as well. The equation - 8 overs | 3 wickets.

OUT! TAKEN! Steven Smith with another catch at first slip and Nathan Lyon has his fourth wicket! This match has just got way too interesting in the last few minutes and it's the visitors who are firmly in control now. Lyon pushes it through quicker and around off. Sajid Khan gets caught on the crease and goes on the back foot. Khan pushes at it with hard hands and with an angled bat. The ball goes off the outside edge and Smith takes another sharp catch. Australia need 3 wickets to win now with 8 overs still remaining in the day.
Commentary.Howout: c Steven Smith b Nathan Lyon

Commentary.Commentary: Tossed up, outside off. Khan pushes it away onto the off side.
Fuller ball, close to the off stump. Khan blocks it out.

FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries and this game just keeps on getting more and more bizarre. On off, Khan with an uppish push past silly mid off and the timing is too good. The ball races away into the fence.
FOUR! Sajid Khan having a bit of fun out there. Tossed up on off, Khan goes down on one knee and slogs it away into the mid-wicket fence.
Flatter, around off. Khan goes back and across and keeps it down towards point.
Cummins bowls this one really short and wide. Rizwan goes chasing after it but misses.
FOUR! This is banged in short on off. Fast hands from Mohammad Rizwan as he gets right on top of the bounce and muscles it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Slanted into middle and leg, keeping a bit low. Rizwan defends it towards short mid-wicket.
Around off, this is blocked out towards covers.
FOUR! Wow! Pitched up, on of. Mohammad Rizwan with a beautiful cover drive through the infield and the ball races away to the fence.
Good-length on off. Rizwan taps it back onto the deck.

Shorter this time, Rizwan pushes it through covers off the back foot and picks up a single.
Drifted onto the pads, Rizwan goes on the back foot and keeps it out on the leg side.
On off, Rizwan leans in to defend.

Excellent shot but just for a single. Full and outside off, driven nicely through covers and the ball just doesn't have the legs to reach the ropes. It shouldn't have been an easy three but Sajid Khan pulled up a bit and they could get only one.
On a length, around off and turning back in. Khan dabs it down to short leg.
Well, Lyon will continue with the new ball!
Pitched up on middle and at 144.5 clicks. Rizwan pushes it firmly back towards the bowler who does well to get a hand on it. Dot to end and Rizwan fails to retain the strike.
FOUR! Full again, outside off. Mohammad Rizwan leans in and thrashes it through covers for a glorious boundary.

Pitched up, on off. Rizwan defends it out.
Back of a length, outside off. Mohammad Rizwan lifts his bat and lets it go.
The third new ball is available and Australia waste no time to take it. Mitchell Starc steams in with the new ball and bowls an inswinging yorker, on middle. Mohammad Rizwan pushes it to mid off.

No hat-trick for Nathan Lyon but he has done his job and Australian players are all re-energized now. Lyon drags the length short and Sajid hangs back to keep it out. The third new ball is now due. Will Cummins take it straightaway?

OUT! TAKEN! What is happening out there? Is there a late twist in the tale? Nathan Lyon has been toiling away for about 50 odd overs and finally, he has his say in this Test match. Lyon drifts it into the pads, the ball turns away a bit after pitching. Faheem Ashraf looks to defend it with an angled bat and the ball goes off the outside edge towards first slip. Steven Smith takes a really good low catch and the visitors will now believe. Lyon is on a hat-trick and Sajid Khan is the new man in.
Commentary.Howout: c Steven Smith b Nathan Lyon

Commentary.Commentary: Faheem Ashraf is the new man in. Well, at this one point one might have thought the teams would shake hands but the rule states that the teams have to play a minimum of 75 overs or till 5.30 pm IST (12 pm GMT). 75 overs are done but there's still around 15 minutes left for STUMPS to be called that is if the teams agree.

OUT! CAUGHT! Nathan Lyon gets the better of Babar Azam! A high-class innings comes to an end. Babar Azam walks off with just 4 runs short of his double ton. Would have been an elusive double hundred but wasn't to be. Heartbreak for him, heartbreak for the fans and the Karachi crowd is stunned. They are up on their feet and give him a huge applause which he deserves. Coming to the ball, it was a loopy delivery from Lyon, on off. Babar Azam pressed forward and tried to defend. Got an inside edge onto the pad and the ball lobbed in the air towards short leg where Marnus Labuschagne took it with both hands. Is that the opening Australia were looking for? Mind you that the new ball is around the corner.
Commentary.Howout: c Marnus Labuschagne b Nathan Lyon

As the clock ticks past 5 pm IST (11.30 am GMT), umpire Aleem Dar signals the start of the final hour of play. We might not be far away from the end of the Test match now.

On middle, Mohammad Rizwan makes room and punches it towards covers.

Given the fact that the required rate is well above 6 runs an over, it looks highly unlikely that Pakistan will in reality be able to chase the target down. The visitors too need 6 more wickets to win which seems a difficult task in itself with two set batters out there. At the end of the 157th over, drinks will be taken and the final hour of the Test match will begin. At that point, the two captains can decide to shake hands and call it a day but Pakistan might not do that, atleast not until their skipper reaches his double-ton. Pat Cummins though might be keen on calling it a day as he wouldn't to further tire his side with the next Test match coming up in just 4 days.

On the pads, worked to mid on for a run.

Full and on off, blocked.

Slower through the air, on off. Blocked out.

Loopy ball, outside off. Mohammad Rizwan lunges forward and knocks it towards covers for a single.

Drinks! Well, no one was expecting this. Everyone thought that the Aussies will press the issue in the final session in order to get a grip on the match but both Mohammad Rizwan and Babar Azam came out with intent and took on the spinners. There are still 21 overs left to play and Pakistan need 134 runs more to win. They could now approach this as a T20 game with two set batters out there. This though will come with risks and Australia might get a few chances. The pendulum has definitely shifted and the visitors might have to settle for a draw at the best or else they might end up letting the match slip out of their grasp completely.

Session Summary - 26 overs, 56 runs, 1 wicket. The wicket of Abdullah Shafique right on the cusp of Lunch opened the gates for Australia and post-Lunch, Fawad Alam did put up a small fight but Pat Cummins bowled his heart out and he got his man. Babar Azam has looked strong as ever and surpassed 150 in the process while Rizwan has come out positive and is showing good support. Both the batters have survived a handful of close shaves but what is important for Pakistan is that they are still at the crease. The pressure is still on Pakistan to survive till the end of the day's play. The equation now -  196 runs | 36 overs | 6 wickets. Australia's hustle to get a breakthrough and Pakistan's resistance on such a pitch is only making things spicier. A Pakistan win is out of the question now but the other two are still on the cards. Which will it be? Join us at 3.30 pm IST (10 am GMT) for the final session to find out.

An engrossing session of Test cricket in which 63 runs were scored and one wicket fell right towards the end of the session. Still, plenty of time left in this Test match for either side to push for the win but realistically the visitors have more of a chance of getting a win but another draw looms large. A very important post-Lunch session coming up in a few minutes time. Stay tuned.

The Aussie bowlers probed and probed without any results but a stroke of genius from the skipper right on the brink of the Lunch break has completely shifted the momentum of the Test match. The visitors still need 7 wickets in two sessions for the win but given that the ball is reversing a fair bit at the moment, both Starc and Cummins will look to make the most use of it right after the interval. Mitchell Swepson took some time to get his line and length up to the mark but Nathan Lyon did bowl really well. The two pacers though hold the key and if they allow the new batters to settle in, the match will keep slipping out of their hands. More than 60 overs to go and that's enough time to get 7 wickets if we go by how the Aussies bowled in the first innings but they need to keep probing and not try to do a bit too much with the ball.

It's time for the Lunch break on the final day of this Test match and things have surely become interesting with Abdullah Shafique getting out just a few minutes before the break. For the most part of the first session though, Babar Azam and Abdullah Shafique looked well in control. Babar did look a bit edgy throughout the session but they weren't mightily troubled by pace or by spin. The pair added on 58 runs today and overall they shared a partnership of 228 runs which has seen Pakistan get to a comfortable position. With 252 runs more needed for victory, it seems a bit out of reach for the hosts and they will now look to negotiate the final day. Babar Azam holds the key here because he is the set batter and he needs to ensure that whoever is batting with him, just plays steadily.

Drinks! Well, it's been a fairly comfortable first hour for the Pakistani batters with both Babar Azam and Abdullah Shafique starting to get a few runs as well. Mitchell Starc and Pat Cummins bowled with pace and intent early on but weren't able to create many chances and the longer the match goes on, the more frustrated the Aussie bowlers are getting. They must believe that it's just a matter of getting one wicket and that could change the momentum considerably. Pakistan though will look to do more of the same. They need 282 runs to win and it will be interesting to see if they do go for the win.
Fuller in length, sliding onto the pads. Abdullah Shafique flicks it straight to backward square leg.
On middle, turned to mid-wicket by Shafique.
On off again, blocked out.
Around off, pushed towards cover.

The umpires though just want to make sure and go upstairs. The soft signal is not out and the replay shows that the ball cleared bounced and then went into the clutches of Marnus Labuschagne.

On off. Blocked out.

Nathan Lyon (22-4-50-1) to bowl for the first time today.

On off, blocked out.

Quicker this time, around off. Azam makes the block.

On off and nipping back in. Azam plays a solid defensive shot.

Bonus runs and Abdullah Shafique has his first runs of the day. Angled into the body, Shafique dabs it down to mid-wicket for a quick run. David Warner has a pop at the bowler's end but Shafique is well in. The ball hist the stumps and rolls towards the fence as there's no one backing up. The batters get a couple of additional runs. The 200 is up for Pakistan.

Around the off pole, left alone.

Angled into middle and leg. Blocked out.

Angling into middle at 145 clicks. Azam gets right behind the line of the ball to make the block.
Sliding into middle and leg, Azam works it well in front of square on the leg side and picks up a couple of runs.
Right on the money! Around off and just tailing in a bit. Babar Azam manages to keep it out.
A touch fuller, around off. Shafique looks to drive but gets it off the inner half of the blade and the ball goes nowhere.
Around the top of middle. Shafique blocks it out.
A bumper now, over middle and leg. Abdullah Shafique sways his head away from the line of the ball.
Length, at 142 clicks and around the hips. Shafique defends it towards mid-wicket.
Close to the off stump, zipping through to the keeper as Shafique makes another leave.
Good-length ball, over leg stump. Azam plays it with soft hands towards short cover and sets off for a single. Good running.
Another pacy delivery, full and attacking the stumps. Shafique stays solid in defense.
A length ball, sliding into middle and leg. Shafique keeps it out.
Babar Azam gets his first runs of the day. On off, dabbed down towards point for a quick single.
Cummins tries to skid one through at 143 clicks but Azam does well to defend it out.

Angled into middle at around 140 clicks. Babar Azam blocks it out solidly.
Pat Cummins to bowl from the opposite end.
On leg stump, Shafique dabs it back onto the deck off the back foot.
Pitched up, around off and Shafique lets it through to the keeper.
WIDE! Full and very wide, beyond the tramline.
This one zipped through! Full and outside off. Shafique makes another leave and Alex Carey collects the ball around head height.
On a good length over off stump. Shafique gets right behind the line of the ball to block.
A length ball, in that channel around off and the ball just holds its line. Shafique makes a watchful leave.
This is pitched up, around off and there's bit of an away shape on it. Shafique leaves it alone.

We are set for the play to begin on Day 5! The Australian team is seen in a huddle as the overnight batters for Pakistan, Babar Azam and Abdullah Shafique take guard. Mitchell Starc is raring to go with the ball.

At 21/2, it looked so good for Australia and a win seemed on the cards but Shafique and Azam dropped their anchors. Both the batters had answers to everything that was thrown at them and stitched an unbeaten stand of 171 where Azam notched up his 6th Test ton while he found an able partner in Shafique who is also approaching his milestone. Australia didn't find much reverse swing with the first new ball and their spinners also bowled in the rough but to no avail. The second new ball is only two-overs old and they would want to make early inroads now. Can Australian bowlers repeat what they did in the first innings? Or will Pakistan drag this to the final session? Stay tuned for all the drama. The first session will begin shortly.

A warm welcome to Day 5 of the second Test between Australia and Pakistan. This Test is hanging right in balance and the final day is going to be a cracker. The equation is 314 runs in 90 overs. Pakistan will most likely try to salvage a draw rather than go for a win while Australia would certainly like to hunt for a win as they know it's very much possible. Let's see how the day pans out.
... Day 5, Session 1 ...

The equation is simple. A day to play out for a draw for Pakistan. If they want to win it, they’ll need to score another 314 runs. Australia need 8 wickets. All to play for to what promises to be an exciting day. Do join us at 10.30 am IST (5 am GMT). But do not forget to tune in early for the build-up. Till then, adios!

Babar Azam is up for a quick chat. He says that this one means a lot. Tells that the team needed it. Mentions that the plan was to build a long partnership and take this deep. Adds that the match isn't over as it's a big day tomorrow. Mentions they'll look to continue with the way they played today. Tells that they have practiced against some reverse swing bowling and they try to play it late and closer to the body. Informs that it's the same plan for tomorrow and they want to extend this partnership for as long as possible.

Australia tried it their all in the last session but just couldn’t find the breakthrough. Swepson was excellent, he was the only one who caused all the problems but was a tad unlucky. The wicket also seemed to have eased out or maybe the old ball became a lot easier to face. However, the good thing for the Aussies is, the ball is new, they’ll come fresh on Day 5, the wicket is expected to deteriorate even more but they’ll need to break this stand early. The new ball is their best chance.

Have to credit Azam abd Shafique for the grit, determination and fight they have shown. Azam clearly showing why he is one of the best going around and Shafique showing that he belongs at this level. Pakistan could not lose a lot of wickets heading in Day 5 and they have lost just the two. However, there are another 90 overs pending and they’ll have to continue the good work.

End of an attritional day of Test cricket! Pakistan will be mighty pleased with how it panned out. A wicket-less session in the last one has seen them have a real chance of drawing this game. Yes, an outside chance of winning it too but just being a little realistic.

TOP EDGE AND OVER WARNER AT SHORT FINE! Hundred for Azam. Cometh the hour cometh the man. Don’t remember the last time he scored a ton in a Test, he was due and has come off at the right time. A knock of high quality. His side needed someone to step up, they had their backs against the wall and it is then skipper who leads from the front. A wicket where the ball is staying low, turning, bouncing, he has played so fluently. A knock for the ages. He though needs to go on for longer, this is only half the job done. He plays a sweep to this ball down the leg side. It goes over short fine leg. Warner runs after it, dives and keeps it down to two. Takes his helmet off and soaks in the applause.

That one keeps low! Pat Cummins can't believe his luck. Good-length ball, on off. Babar Azam gets an inside edge to fine leg for a single. Babar Azam on 99!

Relentless stuff from Green but solid from Azam! On off, Azam gets right behind the line and defends.
Good length and on off, this is kept out.
Another over goes by! On middle, AS leans forward and pushes it back to the bowler.
Flatter and on middle, Shafique works it to short leg.
Angled into the pads, this is worked on the leg side for one.
Tossed up on off, defended.
Flatter and on off, pushed to cover.
That almost sneaks through. Shafique comes down the track. He does not get to the pitch of it but does well to play it with the spin through mid-wicket for one.
A harmless nut to end! Down the leg side. Azam looks to flick but misses.
Solid again! On middle, this is played to mid on.
Probably misreads the length. This is a lot fuller and on off, Azam is rooted to his crease as he blocks.
Another one on middle, kept out well.
An inswinger, coming in from around middle, Azam plays it right under his eyes.

FIFTY! Floats it up, outside off. Babar Azam rocks back and pushes it to the off side for a single. Played a lone battle in the first innings and is playing a fine knock in the second innings as well. His 20th Test fifty! Abdullah Shafique comes up to him to congratulate. The crowd erupts as well to give him a huge cheer.
Outside off, the ball keeps a little low. Abdullah Shafique works it to mid on for one.
Loopy ball, on off. Kept out.
Tosses it up, wide outside off. Babar Azam leans and crunches his drive to wide of deep cover for one.
Flighted delivery, outside off. Easily worked down the ground to long on for a run.
Nathan Lyon to operate from the other end.
Short, outside off. Azam decides to leave it untouched.
Length ball, on off. Abdullah Shafique dabs it to deep backward point for one.
Short of a length, the ball stays low. Abdullah Shafique sways away and lets it go.
Good-length ball, on off. Abdullah Shafique stands tall and defends it back to the bowler.
Length ball, on middle. Abdullah Shafique turns it to mid-wicket.
Short ball, on off. Babar Azam pulls it to deep square leg for a single.

We are back for the final session! Out comes Abdullah Shafique and Babar Azam to continue their innings. Australian players walk out to the middle as well. Cameron Green to start with the ball. Let's go...
... DAY 4, SESSION 3 ...

Australia on the other hand, will be disappointed they could not pick another wicket after getting one early. They could have had Shadfique had Smith held on. Except for that chance, they have struggled to trouble the two batters. There is not a lot on offer for them apart from a couple of balls staying low. The revers swing is not as much as it was in the first innings. They though have to continue to be patient. Another intriguing session awaits. Do join us for the final session which will begin at 3.30 pm IST (10 am GMT).

The Pakistan fight back continues! A session quite similar to the first one for them. They lost Ali early but then Azam led the fight back along with Shafique. We though saw a lot more intent from the two batters as they have managed to score at a decent rate in this session. Runs though is surely not what is playing on their mind at the moment and they would hope they can play out another session without losing a wicket.
Short of a length, outside off. Abdullah Shafique pushes it to the off side. THAT WILL BE TEA ON DAY 4!
Short and angling down leg, Shafique ducks under that one.
Full and on off, Abdullah Shafique with a solid front foot defence.
A wide yorker, outside off. The ball shoots up after hitting the footmark. Abdullah Shafique leaave it alone. Alex Carey does well to collect it moving to his right.
Back of a length, on off. Abdullah Shafique defends it from the crease.
Full and outside off, Abdullah Shafique lets it sail through.
Full and on middle, defended to mid on.
Short of a length, outside off. Left alone.

FOUR! Put away! Short ball, outside off. Babar Azam stands tall and pulls it over mid-wicket. Just over the fielder and the ball races away to the fence. The hosts have done a brilliant job with this partnership to deny Australia any more wickets after the Azhar Ali break!
Fuller, on off. Azam defends.
On a length, on off. Azam blocks it out.
Full and angling down leg, that one keeps low as well as. Babar Azam misses his flick. It goes through to the keeper.
Full and on middle, Shafique plays a good defensive shot.
Very full, outside off. Kept out to the off side.

FOUR! Starc errs in his line and bowls it down leg, Abdullah Shafique tickles it to fine leg. Alex Carey dives to his left but could not get his hands on it. The ball races away to the fine leg fence.
Full and on leg, Shafique turns it towards mid-wicket.
Full and outside off, Shafique defends it towards mid off.
A yorker, on off, angling in. Abdullah Shafique digs it out.
Very full and on the leg stump, Babar drives it towards mid on.
Full and on off, nudged to mid on.

Full and down the leg again, Azam misses his tuck and the keeper manages to glove it towards short fine leg this time.
FOUR! Another boundary! Short and on middle, Babar Azam makes room and punches that away through the covers and the ball races away to the fence.
Full and on middle, Babar Azam drives but hits it to the silly point fielder.
FOUR BYES! Way down the leg side, stays low as well. Babar Azam misses his sweep. Alex Carey tries to stop it with his legs but could not do so. The ball races away to the fine leg fence.
Full and on middle, blocked.
Full and sliding down leg, Babar Azam tickles it to fine leg for a brace.

On middle, blocked.

On the pads, defended.
SIX! Abdullah Shafique takes the aerial route! Full and on off, Abdullah Shafique shimmies down the track and gets to the pitch of the ball. Hammers it over long on for a bigige. He moves to 40!
Floated outside off, Shafique prods and blocks it.
Azam with a solid defence.

On off, Abdullah Shafique blocks it to silly point.

On off, blocked.

Short and that one was into the head, Azam somehow manages to get out of the way of that one. Good pacy and a well-directed bouncer!

Huge shout for an lbw but turned down! Length ball, sliding down leg, Abdullah Shafique misses his tuck and gets hit on the pads. Australia appeal but the umpire says no. The ball rolls on the leg side and the batters take a leg bye.

DRINKS! Yet again Pakistan after losing a wicket early on in the session are showing good fight. However, there is still a long, long way to go and they will hope they do not lose another wicket till Tea. The good thing for them is, the ball is not reversing a lot as of now but the odd one is keeping low. Australia on the other hand, are doing well, they have to continue to be patient, the hour could have been a lot better for them had Smith hung onto a catch but they have still done a very good job.
Close! Length and outside off, Abdullah Shafique looks to leave it alone but tries to do so late. It hits the underedge and goes on the bounce to the keeper.
Another run! Runs coming nicely for Pakistan now! Outside off, this is guided through point for one.
Two more! Outside off, Azam guides it through point for two.
He is just not looking to hit it hard! Here too, it is a half volley outside off, Abdullah Shafique just puts bat on ball and guides it through point for one.
Abdullah Shafique is just in the mind set of blocking here. This is a full toss on off, he just puts bat to ball.
Fuller and on middle, it is defended.
Fuller this time and tailing back in. First time in this innings we saw the ball come back in the way it did. Azam plays it to mid on.
Drop and run! Shorter and on off, Abdullah Shafique drops it towards point for one.
FOUR! That has been cracked! Shorter in length and on off, fractionally short actually. Abdullah Shafique pulls it hard over square leg for a boundary.
Fuller and on middle, this is pushed to mid on.
Now takes one as he works it through square leg. This is the thing with Azam, he will look to score.

FOUR! Uppish but just wide! Babar would have been worried for a minute! Shorter and on middle, Azam pulls, he does not get on top of the bounce completely and hence, it goes in the air but wide of mid-wicket for a boundary.
Angled into the pads, Azam nudges it down to fine leg for one.
Angled into the pads, this is worked to mid-wicket.
Fuller and on middle, Azam works it to mid on.
On middle, defended.
Good length and on middle, defended.
He was almost tempted! Outside off, fuller. Azam thinks about going after it but then leaves it alone.

EDGY FOUR! Length and on off, Azam stands tall and looks to defend, he looks to do so by playing it close to his body and also with soft hands. It goes off the outside edge wide of second slip and down to the third man fence. It is also a no ball.

FOUR! Not sure if that is a shot Azam would have been happy with seeing from the other end! It is a length delivery outside off. Abdullah Shafique hangs his bat out, he ends up playing away from the body. It goes more off the outer half down to the third man fence. That could have easily taken the edge and gone to the keeper. Need to leave those.
On the middle stump, Abdullah Shafique plays it back to the bowler.
On the stumps, kept out again.
Solid again! On the stumps, it is defended. There is one odd ball which is staying low but otherwise, the wicket still seems a decent one to bat on especially with the ball not reversing.
Good length and on middle, Abdullah Shafique stays back and defends.
That one stays low! Outside off, no bounce at all. Left alone.

Bowls a yorker now and on off, Azam gets his bat down in time. Not a lot of reverse for both Starc and Cummins. They are getting a little bit of it but nothing like what happened in the first innings.
Good length and on off, Azam blocks.
Shot! Fuller and on off, Azam shows the full face of the bat and strokes it to mid off.

Azam has a poke there! He gets beaten! The around the wicket angle, that is the reason why he played at it. Starc from wide of the crease angles it in, it lands on a crack and then moves away. Azam plays at it away from the body but gets beaten.
Fuller and on off, Azam shows the full face of the bat and plays it to mid off.
From around the wicket, bowls a loosener first up! Down the leg side. Azam looks to flick but misses.
Good leave! This is in the 5th stump channel. Abdullah Shafique watches it and lets it go through to the keeper.
Fuller and on off, Abdullah Shafique shows the full face of the bat and plays it to mid off.
Angled into middle, a little bit of swing into the batter. Abdullah Shafique works it to mid-wicket.
Another one on a length, this time Shafique gets right behind the line and plays it to mid off.
Good length and outside off, left alone.

EDGED AND DROPPED! Steven Smith is the culprit! Cummins almost struck on the very first ball. That should have been taken. This is maybe his second or third dropped catch. This one though was easy. Length and on off, it lands and moves away. Abdullah Shafique pokes at it, it goes off the outside edge. It gets to Smith quickly at first slip who is standing quite close. He fails to hang on. Can Abdullah Shafique make the most of this chance?
Good shot but only one! Outside off, shorter. Abdullah Shafique stays back and slaps it through covers for one.
Flatter and on middle, Abdullah Shafique keeps it out.
On middle, defended.
On the pads, this is worked through square leg for one.
On the pads, Azam looks to flick, the ball turns away. It goes off the leading edge but a soft one towards mid off.
Fuller and on off, Azam drives it hard but to covers.
Angled into the pads, this is worked down to fine leg for one.
Goes short, Azam watches it till the end and then ducks under it.
Gets it to move the other way now, length and on off, it lands and moves away, it is guided through point for one.
Angles it into the pads, Abdullah Shafique looks to flick but misses to get hit on the pads.
Azam moves onto 9 in no time! Around off, Azam guides it through point for one.
Good length and on middle, Azam blocks it out.
Takes one now! On middle, this is worked through square leg for one.
FOUR! Slapped away! First boundary of this innings! Azam won't be blocking everything, he will play his shots. Shorter and outside off, this is slapped through covers for a boundary.
Close again! This lands around leg, Abdullah Shafique looks to defend, it goes off the inside edge past short leg and towards square leg for one.
Well bowled again! Swepson has been really impressive! Gives it flight and lands it on off, it ptches and turns away. Abdullah Shafique looks to defend but it goes off the outer half on the off side.
Tossed up and on off, defended.
Fuller and on middle, Azam works it down to long on and takes one.
Another one outside off, Abdullah Shafique leaves it alone.
Shorter and on middle, Azam pulls it through square leg for one.
On middle, Azam strokes it back towards the bowler.
This one bounces nicely! This is very short, Azam ducks under it. This is not a bad ploy from Green to bang it short like this, one is keeping low and the other is bouncing nicely.

Kept low again! The key here was Abdullah Shafique kept his eyes on the ball unlike Azhar Ali! This is shorter and on middle, Abdullah Shafique has to adjust as this one does not bounce a lot. He pulls it through square leg for one. Not sure if the pull shots are the right way to go on this wicket.
This one comes back in, Abdullah Shafique defends it well. Green is getting some nice movement.

On off, kept out.
Full and on off, played to mid on.

Fraction short around middle and leg, Shafique tucks it into the leg side for one.
Outside off, left alone.
Azam is off the mark! On off, this is pushed towards cover for one.

Babar Azam walks out to bat.

OUT! LBW! That is unplayable! Green himself can't believe he has a wicket that way. What a move to begin with Green as he strikes on just his second ball. He bangs it shorter in length. Ali looks to duck under it, this one just does not bounce at all. It hits Ali near the thigh pad. An appeal and the finger is raised. Both the batters are having a discussion but time runs out. Perfect start for the Aussies. Ultra Edge shows a spike as it passed the glove. Not sure why the review was not taken there. Ali is such a big wicket, really not good from Pakistan, they wasted a review earlier on when it seemed dead out, this time, there were quite a few doubts but the review was not taken. Wondering how Ali did not realise he did not get glove on it, maybe he was just in shock of how low the ball kept there.
A little bit of movement for Green! On middle, it comes back in. This is worked through mid-wicket for one.

Pushes it through but bowls it outside off, left alone.
Attacks the stumps again and it is flatter. Ali plays it back to the bowler.
Another one tossed up and on off, Ali blocks it out.
Well bowled! Mitchell Swepson once again starts off well. Flatter, it lands on middle, spins away a touch. Ali defends it late.
We are back for the middle session! The players are out. Azhar Ali and Abdullah Shafique to continue their innings. Mitchell Swepson to start with the ball.
... DAY 4, SESSION 2 ...

Pakistan will be pleased with how things have gone about so far! They would have loved to enter the break with no wickets down but Azhar and Abdullah Shafique have done well to keep it down to just the one after they lost Imam. Australia on the other hand, have done their part, they have bowled with discipline, they were rewarded early but since then, the Pakistan batters have managed to keep out everything bowled at them. The intentions are clear from Pakistan, block everything, they hardly played with any intent and we expect more of the same as the day goes on. Australia on the other hand, will need to be patient. The wicket is offering something for the bowlers, the ball has started to reverse just a wee bit but STILL, it is a good one to bat on. Another important session coming up at 1.10 pm IST (7.40 am GMT).

Pakistan have taken a review for an LBW. No bat involved says UltraEdge. Ball Tracking shows three reds. The on-field decision will stay. Pakistan burn their review as well.
